name: Module 1 - Introduction to Amazon FBA (Wholesale & Bundling)

blocks.content: If you have never sold anything online before, the world of Amazon can look like a maze of confusing jargon. Let us strip all of that away.

To build a successful business on Amazon, you do not need to own a massive warehouse, you do not need a fleet of delivery trucks, and you do not need to spend your days packing and sending off customer orders.

Amazon has already spent billions of pounds building the most advanced delivery network on the planet. FBA stands for Fulfilment by Amazon. When you use FBA, you are simply renting a tiny corner of their infrastructure.
The Core Concept: Split the Work
An Amazon FBA business is a partnership between you and Amazon. You handle the digital side; Amazon handles the physical side.

The Lean Reality: because Amazon handles the physical shipping, once you have shipped your products to Amazon you can run this entire business from anywhere in the world with nothing more than a smartphone and a laptop.
The Ultimate Superpower: The Prime Badge

There are two ways to sell on Amazon. The first is FBM (Fulfilment by Merchant), where you handle the whole physical chain yourself. You buy the stock, you store it at home or in a small unit, you print the postage labels, you queue at the post office, and you personally answer every customer message when something goes wrong with an order.

It is slow, it is exhausting, and customers do not trust it the way they trust an Amazon shipment. FBM listings show a generic delivery window of three to seven working days. They have no Prime badge, no guaranteed next-day delivery, and no Amazon-backed returns policy. A buyer comparing two identical products at the same price will pick the Prime listing every single time, even when the FBM version is a few pounds cheaper.

This is exactly why the Elite FBA System uses FBA and not FBM. We do not want to be the warehouse, the post office, and the customer service desk all at once. We want to be the buyer and the strategist. FBA hands the entire physical operation over to Amazon's billion-pound logistics network and gives us our time back to focus on what actually moves the business forward: finding the next profitable product.

Mechanically, FBA is very simple. You ship a single box of stock to an Amazon fulfilment centre. Their staff unload it, scan each unit, and check it into your inventory. From that point on, every customer order is picked off the shelf, packed into an Amazon box, shipped under the Amazon brand, and tracked by Amazon's own systems. If a buyer wants to return it, they speak to Amazon, not to you.

The moment your stock arrives at an Amazon FBA warehouse and is scanned in, your products automatically get the Amazon Prime badge. There is no application form, no waiting list, and no extra fee on top of the standard FBA fees you are already paying. Within a few hours, your listings are live and visible to every Prime customer searching for that product.
Tap each unlock below to see why that single badge is the difference between a listing that sells and a listing that does not.
The math behind Amazon FBA is straightforward. You are looking for simple price mismatches in the real world.

You do not need to guess if a product will make a profit. Before you spend a single penny on inventory, you will use free tools to calculate the exact Amazon fees and your exact profit margin. If the math does not work, you walk away.
Most gurus will tell you to order 500 units of a custom product from China, spend £3,000 upfront, and pray it sells. We do not do that here. That is how beginners lose their life savings.
The Elite FBA method is built on a strict Lean, Validate, Scale framework. Click each step below to see how it works in practice.
Amazon FBA is simply a logistics machine. Once you understand how to slide products into that machine safely, the sky is the limit.
Getting products into the Amazon ecosystem requires a specific, orderly sequence. Following these steps correctly ensures that inventory is tracked accurately and processed without warehouse delays.
The Stow Algorithm and Inventory Health

Once your stock lands at the warehouse, Amazon's Stow algorithm splits your items across different physical shelves in the warehouse, and across different regional fulfilment hubs around the country. This ensures that no matter where a customer orders from, your product is always physically close to a picker, maximising delivery speed.
When looking at your Seller Central dashboard, monitoring stock levels across the three statuses below is a daily operational requirement to prevent stockouts or excessive storage fees.

⚠️ The 180-Day Penalty: if your stock sits in a warehouse for more than 180 days, Amazon charges severe Long-Term Storage Fees. This is why we use the Lean Model: we test with 10 to 12 units first. We never risk buying hundreds of units upfront without historical verification.
Behind the Scenes: The 24-Hour Fulfilment Machine

The moment a customer purchases your product, Amazon does not immediately release the funds to your bank account. They hold them in a temporary reserve to ensure there are no immediate returns or chargebacks. Payouts are typically initiated every 14 days.

While you sleep, work your day job, or spend time with family, this flawless automated machine runs 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Tap any stage of the journey below to see what is happening behind the scenes.
Hands-Off Customer Service: Amazon's Automated Front Desk

When you use Amazon FBA, your job as a customer service representative is effectively eliminated. For a lean, individual operator, managing customer messages, tracking updates, and refunds can drain hours from your week. Amazon absorbs this entire infrastructure, acting as your customer service front desk 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
Here is exactly how this hands-off layer operates in the real world.

If a buyer clicks Contact Seller to ask standard tracking questions like "Where is my parcel?" or "When will this arrive?", Amazon's support team intercepts the message. They handle the communication directly using their live carrier tracking data. You never see the message, and you do not have to reply to it.

If a customer decides they no longer want your bundle, or if a product arrives damaged, they initiate a return through their own Amazon buyer dashboard. Amazon instantly issues a return shipping label, handles the refund processing out of your account's gross funds, and instructs the buyer to ship the physical item back to the fulfilment centre.

Once the returned item arrives back at the warehouse, Amazon's staff inspect it. If the item is still pristine and unopened, they automatically put it back onto the shelf as Fulfillable Inventory to be sold again. If the packaging is torn or opened, they mark it as Unfulfillable, allowing you to recall it to your home address to inspect or salvage the components.

⚠️ The Operator Risk (the Return Rate Metric): while this system is completely hands-off, it is not free from risk. Amazon makes returning items incredibly easy for buyers. As an operator, you must track your Return Rate (total returns divided by total units sold) inside your seller dashboard. If you build poor-quality bundles that get damaged in transit, or if your listing images do not match the physical product exactly, your return rate will spike and put your account health at risk.
What the Prime Badge Really Is

Amazon Prime is the most successful paid subscription service ever launched. For a flat annual fee, members get fast and free shipping on hundreds of millions of products, plus video streaming, music, photo storage, exclusive sales events, and a long list of secondary perks. In the UK and the US, more than half of all households now hold a Prime membership.

On a product page, the badge itself looks deceptively small: a blue chevron mark next to the word Prime, usually sitting just above the price. But that tiny symbol is the single most powerful conversion signal Amazon has ever built. It tells the buyer that this item ships fast, it ships free, and if anything goes wrong, Amazon stands behind it personally.

For a third-party seller, the badge is the front door to the customer. Without it, your listing sits behind an invisible wall that millions of Prime buyers never look past. With it, your listing is funnelled into the same trusted pipeline as every other product Amazon recommends.

The badge does the heavy lifting on three different levers at once: trust, search visibility, and pricing freedom. Each one alone would be valuable. Stacked together they are why an FBA listing routinely out-sells a cheaper FBM listing on the same product page.

Customers do not know who you are, and frankly, they don't care. When they see the Prime badge, their trust transfers directly from Amazon to your listing. They know that if the product is late, damaged, or not what they expected, Amazon's customer service will instantly handle it.

Over 80% of Amazon buyers filter search results strictly by "Prime Only." If you handle your own shipping (FBM / Fulfillment by Merchant), your listing becomes completely invisible to Amazon's most active, highest-spending customers.

Non-Prime sellers often have to lower their prices to get noticed. Because Prime members prioritize speed and reliability, they are consistently willing to pay a premium price. You can list a bundle for £19.99 and comfortably out-sell a non-Prime competitor offering a similar single item for less, simply because your product can be on their doorstep tomorrow morning.

Prime membership is not a casual purchase. People who subscribe pay roughly £95 a year up front, and they actively want to use the perks to feel that the subscription has paid for itself. That single psychological shift changes everything about how they shop on Amazon.

They search differently. They filter for Prime first, often without even noticing the toggle is on. They have made Amazon their default starting point for many categories where, a decade ago, they would have used Google or visited a physical shop. And they trust Amazon's recommendations enough to one-click items they have never seen or heard of before.

📈 The Loyalty Loop: a Prime member who uses the badge to find a useful item is more likely to come back next week, more likely to add a second item to their basket, and more likely to leave a positive review. The badge does not just win a single sale; it triggers a repeating loop that compounds over months and years.
There are two official ways for a third-party seller to earn the Prime badge on a listing. In practice, only one of them is realistic for almost every seller, and that is FBA.

The second route, Seller-Fulfilled Prime, technically lets you keep stock at home and still display the Prime badge. In reality, it requires near-perfect on-time delivery from your own warehouse, a strict packaging audit, and continuous performance monitoring that almost no individual seller can sustain. Amazon has also paused new applications to the programme for years at a time to keep quality high.

🎯 The Practical Reality: for the Elite FBA System, the answer is simple. We always use FBA. The Prime badge appears automatically the moment our stock is scanned in, and we never have to worry about losing it because of a slow delivery, a missed dispatch, or a packaging audit.
The Cost of Using Amazon's Machine

Amazon does not store, pack, and ship your inventory out of goodwill. FBA is an elite infrastructure, but it is an infrastructure that will quietly bleed your bank account dry if you do not understand exactly how it charges you.

To protect your cash flow, you must understand the core fee layers deducted from every sale. As an operator, your job is to calculate these costs down to the penny before you spend a single pound on physical inventory. If you guess, you lose.
Every time a customer clicks Buy Now on your listing, Amazon's system instantly calculates and deducts three distinct fee types before the remaining capital hits your account reserve.
Think of this as your finder's fee. Amazon owns the customer data, the traffic, and the checkout platform; you are paying a direct commission for access to their active buyer base.

The Calculation: for almost every everyday category we target in the Elite FBA framework (Grocery, Beauty, Home, Personal Care, and Toys), this is a flat 15% of the total gross amount the customer pays at checkout.

💷 The Catch: this fee is calculated on the total retail price paid. If you sell a custom multipack for £19.99, Amazon instantly takes £3.00 the exact second the transaction processes. You never handle this money; it is sliced off at the point of sale.
2. The FBA Fulfilment Fee (The Logistics Cost)

This is the flat charge for Amazon's robotics and warehouse staff to physically pull your item off its warehouse shelf, track it, pack it into an official Amazon-branded cardboard box, and deliver it to the customer's doorstep.
The Calculation: this is based strictly on the weight and the physical outer dimensions of your finished, pre-packaged bundle. It has absolutely nothing to do with the retail price you charge.

📐 The Operator Rule: when sourcing inventory in physical retail shops, always look at items through the lens of volumetric weight. A bundle that can be packed tightly into a flat polybag or a slim mailer box will always make more money than an awkwardly shaped, hollow, or bulky item.
You are renting high-value physical space inside Amazon's fulfilment centres. This space is measured and billed monthly per cubic foot (roughly 30cm × 30cm × 30cm).

Standard Storage (January to September): a low, highly predictable baseline operating cost. As long as your inventory turns over within our recommended 30 to 45 day window, this fee is negligible and barely impacts your net margins.

Peak Q4 Storage (October to December): during the holiday rush, millions of sellers flood the warehouses with inventory. To prevent gridlock and force slow-moving items out, Amazon triples their monthly storage fees.

🎯 The Operator Rule: if you have dead or unvalidated stock sitting on a warehouse shelf in November, storage fees will swallow your profits. This is exactly why the Elite FBA framework uses a lean setup: we test initial demand with only 10 to 12 units. We never buy hundreds of units upfront to sit around gathering dust and racking up penalty fees.

Amazon breaks products down into incredibly strict dimensional size categories. Moving just 1mm past a size tier boundary can instantly bump your fulfilment fee up by £0.50 to £1.50 per unit. That single millimetre can completely wipe out your projected net profit.

When you are bundling items together physically at your desk (for example, taping a 3-pack of specialised lightbulbs together), you are the manufacturer. How you position, wrap, and bag those items determines their final dimensions.

⚠️ Operator Warning: if you bag items loosely and leave excess plastic flagging out from the sides, Amazon's automated laser scanners (Cubiscan machines) will measure that empty plastic flagging as part of the solid product volume. You will be up-charged into a higher parcel tier for shipping trapped air. Wrap your bundles tight, tap down excess corners, and pack them as densely as humanly possible.
To help you visualise how these fee layers operate in action across different item types, analyse these three distinct operational scenarios based on common retail bundle configurations.

Unit economics is the per-sale profit and loss of a single product. It is the smallest meaningful financial unit in your business. Everything else, from the size of your Q4 storage bill to the speed of your cash compounding, is a downstream consequence of these numbers.

Operators do not look at revenue. Revenue is a vanity figure that hides the cost of running the business. They look at one number: how many pounds are left in their pocket after every single unit is sold, fees deducted, returns absorbed, and storage accounted for. If that number is healthy and repeatable, the business scales smoothly. If it is not, no amount of sales volume will save it.

💡 The Operator Mindset: a £100,000-a-year bundle that nets £0.50 per unit is a tax-only business. A £30,000-a-year bundle that nets £8 per unit is an actual operation. We optimise for the second every single time.
Single Item vs Bundle: The Real Math

The cleanest way to see why this framework works is to compare the per-unit economics of fighting for an existing single-product listing against running your own unique bundle. The figures below are pulled from a representative pair of listings: a generic car sponge sold on a crowded ASIN versus a bundle we built around it.

🎯 The Key Reframe: total Amazon fees on the bundle (£6.00) are only £2.50 higher than the single item (£3.50), yet net profit per unit is more than five times larger. Raising the Average Order Value through bundling makes Amazon's flat logistics fees work for you rather than against you.
The Three Levers of Healthy Bundle Economics

Every bundle in the Elite FBA framework is evaluated against three independent levers. Move any one of them in the right direction and your unit economics improve. Get all three pointing the right way and the bundle compounds into a genuine cash-flow asset rather than a side-project listing.

Before sourcing any bundle, you run it through the floor rule. If the projected per-unit numbers do not clear all four thresholds at the same time on conservative assumptions, the bundle does not get built. This is the line between a hobbyist hunting for any sale and an operator running a real P and L.

⚠️ The Floor Is Not a Goal: hitting £5 net or 30% margin is the minimum threshold to even consider sourcing. A bundle that clears it by a hair will not survive a fee revision, a Q4 storage cycle, or a 5% return rate. Aim well above the floor, then sourcing decisions become easy.

A single bundle running at the floor (around 60 units a month at £5 net) produces roughly £300 of net cash per month. Modest. The compound game is what happens when you have five, ten, or twenty of these running in parallel, each one validated, locked behind a brand registry, and replenished automatically from wholesale.

That is what good unit economics buy you. Not a single windfall but a quietly growing system that gets larger every month with no extra headcount, no extra customer service workload, and no extra retail real estate. Each bundle is an independent cash-flow engine running on the same warehouse infrastructure.
Bundles that look great on a spreadsheet can collapse the moment they hit a real fulfilment centre. The most common failure modes show up in roughly the same shapes every time.

📐 The Tier-Tripping Bundle: the components nest beautifully on paper, but the polybag adds 3mm of slack and pushes the finished pack into the Standard Parcel tier. An extra £1.50 per unit on every sale, forever. Mitigation: measure the prototype with calipers and confirm the tier before sending anything in.

🐢 The Slow-Mover: net £8 per unit looks great until you realise the bundle sells two units a month. Storage fees, return processing, and stockout penalties eat the margin alive. Mitigation: validate velocity in Phase 2 of the blueprint before committing any wholesale capital.

❄️ The Q4 Crusher: a 25% margin in March becomes a 5% margin in November when Amazon triples storage fees. Mitigation: keep margins comfortably above 30% during validation, so peak season pressure still leaves something on the bone.

Unit economics is not a one-off calculation. It is the lens through which every sourcing decision, every wholesale negotiation, and every Q4 inventory buy is filtered. Master it on the validation bundle and the model carries forward to every bundle you build after it.

name: Module 2 - Opening your first Seller Account

blocks.content: Opening an Amazon Seller account seems simple, but it is the first major hurdle where many beginners fail. Amazon's verification bots are ruthless. One typo or mismatched address can result in an immediate suspension before you even list a product.
In this module, we will ensure you get approved on the first try so you can start sourcing immediately.
Amazon offers two selling plans. Here is the golden rule: Start with the Individual plan.
Individual Plan: No monthly fee. You pay £0.75 per item sold. Perfect for the 'Lean' phase.
Professional Plan: £25/month (excl. VAT). Necessary once you sell 35+ items a month or want to win the Buy Box.
You can upgrade to Professional at any time with one click in your Seller Central settings. Save your money while you are learning and sourcing your first products.
CRITICAL: Every single document you provide to Amazon must match EXACTLY. Character for character.

If your bank statement says '123 Main St, Apt 4' and you type 'Apt 4, 123 Main Street' into Amazon, the automated system will reject you. The bots do not have common sense. Copy your address exactly as it appears on your official documents.
Before you click 'Register', gather the following documents. Do not start the process without them.
A valid Passport or Driver's License (Check the expiry date!)
A Bank Statement issued within the last 90 days (Must show your name and address clearly)
A chargeable credit or debit card (Monzo/Starling work fine, but physical high-street banks are preferred if possible)
A dedicated email address (e.g., yourname.fba@gmail.com) so you don't miss important account updates.
Amazon now requires a short video call to verify your identity. This is to stop fraudulent sellers. It takes 5 minutes.
Have your physical ID and printed/digital bank statement ready in your hand.
Ensure you are in a well-lit room with a stable internet connection.
The associate will ask you to hold your ID next to your face and tilt it to show the holograms.
Create your dedicated Amazon email address.
Download your latest bank statement as a PDF.
Register for an Individual Amazon Seller account at sell.amazon.co.uk.
Set up a 2-Step Verification app (like Google Authenticator) to secure your account.
To identify low-risk products or combinations that already have proven demand — such as poor listings, low stock, or missing bundles.
This approach flips the traditional “software-only” model on its head.
Find 3 individual items that sell well on Amazon
Identify 2 potential bundle ideas (complementary items that could be listed together)
Log everything into your Product Research Sheet (name, price, profit, reviews, etc.)
Choose your favourite product idea to use in Module 4 – Creating Your First Listing
Instant proof of demand → if a product is sold in major UK shops, people are already buying it.
Local advantage → most sellers never step outside online tools.
Unique bundles → combining complementary retail products creates your own ASIN and USP.
Low starting cost → you can test ideas with £20–£50 total spend.

You’re in Tesco and notice a shelf of car care products.
Both have separate Amazon listings with steady sales and average reviews.
Neither listing offers a combined “interior cleaning kit.” This is where we shine.
You create a new bundle as:
“Car Care Essentials Duo – Glass Cleaner + Dashboard Wipes”
A clear use-case bundle customers instantly understand
A safe, everyday product that shows how bundling works - without entering sensitive niches like skincare or supplements
📦 Module 4 – Creating Your First Listing (Generic ASIN Method)
It’s time to bring your product idea to life on Amazon, testing demand, keywords and profit margins.
The goal is to get live on Amazon fast and test demand — not to build a brand yet.
Most new sellers wait months trying to design logos and order packaging.
By listing under the “Generic” brand, you can:
✅ Skip GTINs and UPC codes using GTIN exemption
✅ Avoid trademark or Brand Registry requirements
💬 Think of this as your “proof of concept” stage.
Once you confirm sales, then you can form your Ltd company, apply for a trademark, and rebrand the listing under your own name. (Module 6)
Go to Inventory → Add a Product → Create a New Listing
Under Product ID Type → select GTIN Exemption
Tip: When you’ve written your description, paste it into: https://www.sellerapp.com/amazon-product-description-editor.html
Once you have the HTML version, paste this into the Amazon description area.
This ensures that your description is formatted correctly, ensuring that it looks professional and appealing to customers.
Title: Car Care Essentials Duo – Glass Cleaner & Dashboard Wipes (Generic Brand)
You don’t need professional photography yet — just clean, compliant, and clear images.
Pure white background (you can remove background using Canva or Remove.bg)
No watermarks, logos, or text overlays
Show everything included in the bundle
Include 1 image of product + packaging together (Amazon requirement for GTIN exemption)
Use your phone in natural lighting.
A £10 white foam board and daylight can produce excellent photos for testing.
Price for motion, not maximum profit.
When testing Generic listings, your goal is to move stock and learn.
Aim for a small but noticeable gap below similar listings — just enough to attract clicks.
If competitors are at £9.99 → list yours at £8.49 to start.
Once you sell your first 10–20 units and see consistent sales, you can:
Start thinking about branding & packaging for your trademark phase
❌ Using branded items without modification (don’t list “Dettol Bundle” under Generic)
✅ Always create your own ASIN, never hijack an existing one
❌ Forgetting packaging photo (Amazon can reject GTIN exemption)
✅ Keep your packaging simple — plain polybag or small box with an FNSKU label is fine
Apply for GTIN exemption under your chosen category
Take clear photos of your product and packaging
Create a new listing under the Generic brand
Prepare your FBA shipment for Amazon (we’ll cover this next)
You’ve now learned how to create a fully compliant, barcode-free listing under Generic, test your bundle idea, and get real data before investing in a brand.
Next up → Module 5: Turning Proof of Concept Into a Real Brand — where we’ll form your Ltd company, register your trademark, and apply for Brand Registry.
🚚 Module 5 – Sending Your Product to Amazon FBA
It’s time to make your listing real — by sending your product to Amazon’s warehouse and going live for the first time.
FBA (Fulfilled by Amazon) means Amazon stores, picks, packs, and ships your product for you.
You send your inventory to an Amazon warehouse
When someone orders → Amazon handles delivery, returns, and customer service
Low starting effort (you can send as few as 5–10 units)
Get your first units to Amazon, learn the process, and make sure your first FBA shipment is smooth.
Amazon’s golden rule: every product must be barcode-scannable and safely packaged.
All components of the bundle are inside one bag or box
Packaging is plain and professional (no trademarked logos)
Add a small “Sold & Packaged by [Your Name]” sticker if possible
Include FNSKU label (Amazon’s barcode) on the outside of the packaging
After you create your FBA shipment, Amazon will generate a unique barcode (FNSKU) for each SKU.
Regular printer + cut them out  (for small batches)
Each individual product needs its own FNSKU for Amazon to understand what it is — not just the box or bag.
Once your listing exists, you can convert it to FBA and send stock to Amazon.
Go to Inventory → Manage All Inventory
Enter your ship-from address (home or office)
Choose your carrier (Amazon Partnered or own courier).
Place one FNSKU on each unit.
Place one box label (with “FBA” and “UPS” barcodes) on each carton.
Make sure they’re not covered by tape or seams.
Amazon’s partnered UPS service is by far the easiest way to start.
Sending 1 small carton (5 kg) via UPS Partnered:
You can book collection or drop off at any UPS Access Point. Same goes if you choose DPD.
Use strong boxes — no gaps or rattling.
Add bubble wrap or kraft paper for protection.
Never reuse branded boxes (Amazon can reject them).
Avoid mixing products in the same carton (one ASIN/FNSKU per box ideally).
🕒 Lesson 5 – What Happens After You Ship
Your listing status changes from “Inactive – Out of Stock” to “Active.”
Units enter FC (Fulfilment Centre) processing (takes 24–72 hours).
You’ll start seeing your inventory count and Buy Box price live.
Congratulations — you’re now officially selling on Amazon. 🎉
✅ Double-check FNSKU placement before sealing the box.
✅ Always re-check Amazon’s category rules before shipping.
✅ Amazon will reject items that look used, dented, or dirty.
✅ Keep under 63.5 cm (25 in) per side and under 15 kg unless otherwise allowed.
Print and attach FNSKU labels to each unit
Pack your products safely (one ASIN per box)
Create your shipment in Seller Central
💬 Tip: Track your first shipment daily — seeing “Delivered to Fulfilment Centre” is the best motivation you’ll ever get.
🏗️ Module 6 – Turning Proof of Concept Into a Real Brand

You’ve proven people want your product — now it’s time to turn that into something permanent. This is the biggest step in the entire system, and it’s not a one-day job. Expect this phase to take several weeks to a few months. Go slowly, stay organised, and reach out if you’re unsure — I’m happy to guide you through any part of it.
Each stage — company formation, trademark registration, brand approval — has waiting periods built in.
⏳ Don’t rush — treat it like building foundations for the rest of your FBA journey.
🎯 Lesson 1 – Knowing When You’re Ready to Build a Brand
If you’re selling consistently and customers clearly like what you’re offering, you’ve earned the right to build something bigger.
You’ve sold 30 + units of your test product.
You’ve had repeat orders or stable weekly sales.
You understand your fees and margins.
You’ve handled at least one FBA shipment confidently.
If you’re still unsure, message me first — I can help you decide whether to push forward or gather a little more data.
A limited company legally separates you from your business. It’s your “official identity” on Amazon.
Choose a name that reflects your brand direction.
Registered office: home or virtual address.
Wait for your Company Number and Certificate of Incorporation (usually 24 hrs).
Lets you open a business bank account.
Makes Amazon and suppliers treat you as legitimate.
🗣️ If you need help choosing a name or deciding between your own name vs brand name, check with me before submitting.
🏦 Lesson 3 – Setting Up a Business Bank Account
Apply with Starling, Monzo, Tide, or Revolut Business.
Use your company name to match your Amazon account later.
Keeps business income separate from personal.
Adds professionalism when paying suppliers or applying for insurance.
⏳ Banks may take a week or more to approve — don’t panic.
This step gives you ownership of your brand name — no one else can legally sell under it.
Search your brand name — ensure it’s unique.
File your application (£170 + £50 per extra class).
Upload your logo or plain text name.
Wait 8–12 weeks for review and opposition period.
Adds resale and credibility value to your business.
Wrong class → you’ll have to re-file.
🗣️ If you’re unsure which class to choose, ask me before you submit — I can help check your category.
🪪 Lesson 5 – Applying for Amazon Brand Registry
This is where Amazon recognises you as a verified brand owner.
Gives access to Brand Analytics, Vine Reviews, and Sponsored Brand Ads.
Prevents hijackers listing under your ASINs.
💬 If your application gets rejected or delayed, message me — I’ve dealt with most of the common errors before.
Branding makes your store look real. You don’t need to be a designer — just stay consistent.
Logo – simple, clear, readable at thumbnail size.
Colour Scheme – pick 2–3 colours you’ll use everywhere.
Basic Packaging – stickers or printed inserts showing your logo.
A+ Images – lifestyle shots and comparison charts.
Reinforces your brand when you expand into new products.
🗣️ If you want help designing packaging or logo ideas, send them to me for feedback before printing.
💰 Lesson 7 – Upgrading Your Amazon Seller Account
Now that you’re operating as a company, it’s time to upgrade to the Professional Plan (£30 / month).
Seller Central → Settings → Account Info → Upgrade Account.
Save fees if you sell 40 + units / month.
🚀 Module 7 – Scaling Your Brand: PPC, Keywords, Helium 10 & A+ Content
You’re now a registered brand. This module shows you how to make your listing visible, trustworthy, and profitable — using the exact tools real Amazon brands use today.
Before we jump into PPC and keywords, you need to understand two sides of Amazon success:
1️⃣ Visibility — can people find your product?
This is where keywords and PPC come in.
People must SEE your listing before they can buy it.
2️⃣ Conversion — do people buy once they see it?
This is where A+ content, images, reviews, and trust come in.
A listing can fail in two ways:
Lots of traffic but no purchases → conversion problem
Great listing but nobody sees it → visibility problem
I’ll show you how to fix each one step-by-step.
🧱 LESSON 2 — Keywords: The Core of Amazon’s Algorithm
Think of keywords as the “language” Amazon uses to understand what you’re selling.
Amazon doesn’t magically know your product.
It only knows what you tell it through:
Imagine you sell a Car Interior Cleaning Duo.
Amazon won’t automatically connect you to searches like:

You must tell Amazon:
“This is what my product is relevant for.”
If you’re not ranking for the right keywords, nobody can buy your product.
📌 How to find the right keywords (beginner version)
Choose keywords that clearly apply to YOUR bundle
This is the tool that helped me build my company — and it removes guesswork.
Here’s EXACTLY what beginners should use:
